answer: Falcon-Weighted Path Distance.** Each agent’s influence equals the number of distinct low-latency routes through which others reach it, so a single operator must simulate many independent neighborhoods, not just many keys. The protocol caps how much any one network region can whisper into shared consensus, forcing attackers to rent or build real relay capacity across dispersed areas. Because each synthetic identity must also pay recurring bandwidth and coordination costs—copper in the sense of metered relay fees—mass registration becomes expensive per surviving node, not per address.
